segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: though Jesus himself was not baptizing; his disciples were—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he left Judea and set off again for Galilee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He had to pass through Samaria.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of land that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jacob’s spring was there. So Jesus, tired from the journey, sat down just as he was by the spring. It was about the sixth hour.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Give me a drink.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For his disciples had gone off into the town to buy food.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Samaritan woman said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “How is it that you, a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that is saying to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The woman said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, you have no bucket, and the well is deep. So where do you get this living water?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Surely you are not greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, along with his sons and his livestock?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. Rather, the water that I will give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The woman said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, give me this water, so that I will not be thirsty or have to keep coming all the way here to draw.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go, call your husband, and come back here.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The woman answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I have no husband.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You are right to say, ‘I have no husband,’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband. In this you have spoken the truth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The woman said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, I see that you are a prophet.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you people say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Believe me, woman, an hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But an hour is coming, and is now here, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for indeed the Father is seeking such people to worship him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The woman said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I know that Messiah is coming, the one called Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am he, the one speaking to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just then his disciples came, and they were amazed that he was talking with a woman. Yet no one said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What do you want?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: or

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why are you talking with her?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the woman left her water jar, went off into the town, and said to the people,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did! Could this be the Messiah?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They went out of the town and were making their way to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Meanwhile the disciples kept urging him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbi, eat.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I have food to eat that you do not know about.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the disciples said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely no one has brought him something to eat?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to complete his work.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do you not say, ‘Four months more, and then the harvest comes’? Look, I tell you, lift up your eyes and see the fields: they are white for harvest. Already

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the reaper is receiving wages and gathering fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For in this the saying is true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I sent you to reap what you have not labored for. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He told me everything I did.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them, and he stayed there two days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And many more believed because of his word,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they said to the woman,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We no longer believe because of what you said, for we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this truly is the Savior of the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After the two days he left there for Galilee,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for Jesus himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen all that he had done in Jerusalem at the festival, for they too had gone to the festival.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. Now there was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come down and heal his son, for the boy was about to die.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The royal official said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, come down before my child dies.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go; your son lives.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and set off.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still on his way down, his slaves met him and told him that his boy was alive.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he asked them the hour at which the boy had begun to get better, and they told him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the father realized that it was at that very hour that Jesus had said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Your son lives.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he himself believed, and his whole household.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was now the second sign that Jesus did, after he had come from Judea to Galilee.

notes.note: The Greek text followed here reads “Jesus”; many manuscripts, including some early ones, read “the Lord” instead. Editors are divided over which is original. The meaning of the sentence is unaffected.

The Greek word here and in verse 14 means a spring or source of flowing water. The woman in verses 11–12 uses a different word that means a dug well. Most translations have “well” throughout, but keeping the two words apart shows that Jesus’s “spring of water” in verse 14 picks up the narrator’s word, not the woman’s.

Hours were normally counted from sunrise, so the sixth hour is about noon, the hottest part of the day. A minority of scholars think John counts from midnight or noon, which would make it about six in the evening; most do not. The “seventh hour” in verse 52 is, on the usual reckoning, about one in the afternoon.

The verb can mean to associate with someone, which is the traditional reading. It can also mean to use something together with someone, in which case the point is that Jews would not share a drinking vessel with Samaritans for reasons of purity. Scholars are divided, and the second reading suits the scene well. The sentence is the narrator’s aside and is absent from a few early manuscripts.

“Living water” was the ordinary expression for fresh, flowing water from a spring or stream, as opposed to still water in a cistern. The woman takes it in that everyday sense, which is why she asks where he will get it. Jesus means water that gives life, and in the Scriptures God himself is called a fountain of living water.

The mountain is Gerizim, which rises above the site of the conversation. Samaritans held that it, not Jerusalem, was the place God had chosen for worship. A Samaritan temple had stood there until the Judean ruler John Hyrcanus destroyed it in the late second century BC.

Greek manuscripts do not distinguish capital letters, so “spirit” here could be the human spirit, or a spiritual mode of worship, or God’s own Spirit. The lowercase matches “God is spirit” in verse 24. Many interpreters think John means worship made possible by the Spirit that Jesus gives, and that “spirit and truth” form a single idea.

“Messiah” is a Semitic word meaning “anointed one” and “Christ” is its Greek translation. The explanation is probably the evangelist’s gloss for Greek readers, as at 1:41, though the Greek does not mark it off from the woman’s words. “Christ” is kept here because the verse is giving the Greek equivalent of the term.

notes.traditional: I that speak unto thee am he
notes.note: The Greek is simply “I am, the one speaking to you.” In context it means “I am he,” that is, the Messiah she has just mentioned. The same two words are used for God’s self-declaration in the Greek version of Isaiah and are used pointedly by Jesus later in John (8:58). Many scholars hear that overtone here; others take it as plain self-identification.

The Greek is “the Christ,” used here as a title for the expected anointed figure and not as a name. “Messiah” conveys that to a modern reader, and several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels. The form of the woman’s question in Greek is tentative; it does not assert that he is.

Ancient manuscripts had no punctuation, so “already” can end this sentence (“white for harvest already”) or begin the next (“Already the reaper is receiving wages”). The Greek edition followed here takes it with what follows, though the word stands at the end of verse 35. Both readings have support among translators and commentators.

It is disputed which place John means. In the other Gospels the saying refers to Nazareth in Galilee, but here the Galileans welcome Jesus in the next verse. For that reason some take the homeland to be Judea or Jerusalem, which he has just left. Others think the Galilean welcome, based only on signs, is itself the lack of honor.
The Greek word denotes people who were owned, not hired staff. “Servants” is the traditional English, and it softens this. A royal official’s household would ordinarily have included slaves.
